impact:
N-009 §3 requires every surface to declare a disappearance policy so coverage can tell producer eviction from data loss. For `claude-blocks` no such policy can be honestly declared in T-025, and two review rounds killed two different attempts.

WHAT IS MEASURED (owner's real corpus, 2026-08-04):
- `ccusage blocks --json` returns 148 rows spanning 2026-07-01 → 2026-08-05 (~35 days).
- `--since` IS honored: `--since 20260801` returns 19 rows from 2026-08-01.
- But `--since 20251211` returns the SAME 148 rows from 2026-07-01 — asking for more does not produce more.
- Over the identical corpus, `all-daily` returns 190 rows back to 2025-12-11, and codex-daily/codex-sessions/claude-instances likewise span the full 237 days.

So blocks holds materially less history than every sibling surface built from the same transcripts, and the caller cannot widen it.

WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, AND THIS IS THE POINT: that any particular row vanished because the producer evicted it. A single observation proves truncation EXISTS; it cannot prove a given trailing recession is authorized.

TWO ATTEMPTS, BOTH REJECTED IN REVIEW:
1. A declared retention horizon (30 d). Rejected round 1: it permits real rows to vanish the day after the constant on no evidence the producer prunes then, and the per-publish volume cap meant to bound it was RESETTABLE, so repeated individually-legal losses erode everything while every transition passes.
2. `MirrorsProducerWindow` — trailing recession treated as definitional, with interior gaps and leading-edge loss still refusing. Rejected round 2: it MOVES the assumption rather than removing it. A candidate containing only the newest surviving block is a valid trailing suffix, so accidental loss of every older block passes. Worse, non-empty → empty has no honest rule at all: a missing source and a legitimately expired window are indistinguishable, yet refusing empty candidates wedges a user who has simply been quiet.

The remaining honest option inside T-025 is `NoDisappearance` for blocks — but that wedges the store the first time the window legitimately slides, which the measurement says it will, and the refusal has no escape short of a reset that cannot help.

THIS IS AN OWNER DECISION. The options:
(a) ACCEPT BOUNDED TRAILING LOSS on blocks explicitly, and record it as accepted rather than discovered — the store mirrors ccusage's current window and does not attest completeness for this surface. Consistent with N-009 §3's own derived-cache-purity paragraph ("the CLI's blocks view never showed more than ccusage's current window, so neither does the store"), but it must be a decision, not an inference a planner draws from that sentence.
(b) EXCLUDE claude-blocks from coverage attestation entirely — it is replaced wholesale each publish and coverage simply does not apply. Requires deciding what `sourceVersion` for it then attests.
(c) OBTAIN PRODUCER-SUPPLIED WINDOW/RETENTION METADATA bound to each response — the only option that makes mirroring safe by construction. ccusage does not expose this today, so it is an upstream ask.
(d) RUN A CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT establishing the pinned producer's eviction contract — deliberately construct a corpus and observe what the pinned ccusage version drops and when. This is a real experiment someone can run and it would convert the premise from assumed to witnessed.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) as the immediate unblock, with (d) as the durable fix. (a) is the only option that is both honest and non-wedging, and it matches what the CLI has always shown users. But accepting data loss is not a planner's call.

CORRECTION AFTER DISPOSITION REVIEW — WHAT DOES NOT COUNT: an earlier version of this issue offered "hold until T-012's longitudinal observation" as a fourth option. That is WRONG and is withdrawn. Two observations separated in time can show that blocks RECEDED; they cannot distinguish authorized producer eviction from accidental source loss, so passive observation does not satisfy L-006 and cannot authorize a disappearance policy. T-012 may still collect the transitions — that is worth doing — but the result is DIAGNOSTIC EVIDENCE feeding option (d), never a premise in its own right. Recorded explicitly because the distinction is exactly the defect class this project keeps hitting: observing a property and using it as though a stronger one had been proven.

BLOCKS: T-025 item 3's registry entry for claude-blocks. Combined with ISS-090 (surface 6), two of the six surfaces have no specifiable policy, and N-009 §1 fixes the key set per SCHEMA_VERSION — so the exact-key schema cannot be completed either.

Found across T-025 plan review rounds 1 and 2, and sharpened by the round-3 disposition review (codex session 019fcfc4).
title: No witnessable disappearance policy exists for claude-blocks: the surface demonstrably holds less history than its siblings, but nothing available attests WHY rows vanish
